newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Gaelic Games-Meath and Mayo limber up for replay.
newsitem.headline: Gaelic Games-Meath and Mayo limber up for replay.

text.p: Meath and Mayo face each other again in Sunday's All-Ireland football final replay at Croke Park after a last-minute point earned Meath a dramatic draw in the teams' first encounter on September 15.

The crucial point, scored by defender Colm Coyle just before the final whistle, produced a 0-12 to 1-09 scoreline to save the day for Meath and give them another chance to claim the coveted Sam Maguire trophy.
Both teams have made just one change for Sunday's game.

Meath's Colm Brady, who made a big impression when he came on as a substitute in the drawn match, replaces Evan Kelly as right corner forward in the first change Meath selectors have made in the championship this year.
Mayo have also replaced their right corner forward, introducing Anthony Finnerty for David Nestor.
It is 30 years since a Connacht side won the All-Ireland final and Mayo are hungry to take Sam Maguire back to the west.
Manager John Maughan was upbeat as the big day approached. "We are looking forward to the replay," he said ealier this week. "Our players are in good shape, physically and mentally."

Mayo won the last of their three football titles 45 years ago when they beat Meath in the 1951 final. The county last contested an All-Ireland final in 1989 when they were beaten by Cork on a scoreline of 0-17 (17) to 1-11 (14).
This year, Mayo defeated London, a team mostly made up of expatriots, Roscommon and Galway to secure the Connacht title before going on to beat well-fancied Munster champions Kerry in the semi-final.
Meath, who have made a habit in recent times of staging late rallies to win or draw matches they looked set to lose, beat Cork in a 1988 replay to win their last All-Ireland title.
In this year's campaign, they defeated Carlow, Laois and champions Dublin to lift the Leinster title and triumphed over Ulster champions Tyrone to qualify for the All-Ireland final.

MAYO, 1-John Madden; 2-Kenneth Mortimer, 3-Kevin Cahill, 4-Dermot Flanagan; 5-Pat Holmes, 6-James Nallen, 7-Noel Connelly (Captain); 8-Liam McHale, 9-David Brady; 10-James Horan, 11-Colm McMenamon, 12-Maurice Sheridan; 13-Anthony Finnerty, 14-John Casey, 15-Ray Dempsey.
